paper.title: Focusing Where Vision Matters: Selective Training for Large Vision Language Models via Visual Information Gain

claims.paper_claim: Visual Information Gain is defined as a perplexity-based log-ratio measuring how much image conditioning reduces answer uncertainty.
VIG is decomposable to sample and token levels, enabling fine-grained detection of visually grounded tokens.
Examples on MS-COCO show positive VIG for matching images, smaller positive VIG for partially grounded images, and negative VIG for conflicting images.
Token-level analysis identifies high positive loss differences for visually grounded words and near-zero or negative differences for weakly visual tokens.
VIG-guided selective training prioritizes high-VIG samples and tokens to improve visual grounding while reducing supervision.
Experiments compare VIG-guided selective training against full-data and existing methods for overall performance, data efficiency, and language-bias mitigation.
